_comment: DRAFT v2 PREPARED 21 Nov 2026 from the founder's confirmed status (Czech identified person) and the legal & tax review of 21 Nov 2026 (T1-T14). First-sale scope: Czech B2B only. NOT the accountant's written answer and NOT loaded by the code: config/tax-policy.json stays unapproved until the accountant confirms each line in writing and the approval block is filled with a real person, role, date and filing reference. Every decision below is a proposal to confirm, correct or replace; nothing in it is a representation that the tax authority has verified anything.

seller.address: Školská 1736/12, Nové Město, 110 00 Praha 1, Czech Republic
seller._note: vatId = DIČ shown on the published legal pages. Use it only if it matches the actual registration; the accountant confirms it against the registration certificate and fills vatEffectiveFrom from that document. Do not represent the status as verified by the tax authority until then.

decisions.T1_vatStatus: PROPOSED: Colleague AI s.r.o. is treated as an identified person (identifikovaná osoba, § 6g-6l ZDPH), DIČ CZ29540852, from [vatEffectiveFrom - from the registration certificate], not a VAT payer. It charges no Czech VAT on ordinary domestic supplies. It files a VAT return only for periods with reverse-charge transactions and an EC Sales List (souhrnné hlášení) for services supplied to EU businesses. EVIDENCE NEEDED: registration certificate or official confirmation with the effective date (founder); accountant's written confirmation.
decisions.T2_euBusinessWithVatId: PROPOSED: Place of supply = the customer's member state (§ 9(1) ZDPH / Art. 44 Directive 2006/112/EC); the customer accounts for VAT where Art. 196 applies. Document without Czech VAT, with both VAT IDs and the note 'Daň odvede zákazník / Reverse charge - Art. 196 Directive 2006/112/EC'; reported in the EC Sales List for the period. FIRST SALE: HOLD (manual handling; VAT ID and business status verified first). Kept in the matrix so that switching to SELL later is a configuration change, not a redesign.
decisions.T3_domesticBusiness: PROPOSED: Supply by an identified person to a Czech business: no Czech VAT. The document is an invoice (faktura), not a daňový doklad, and carries the note 'Dodavatel není plátcem DPH; je identifikovanou osobou (§ 6g zákona č. 235/2004 Sb.). / The supplier is not a VAT payer; it is an identified person. No Czech VAT is charged.' Never print reverse-charge wording on a domestic invoice. SELL once T1 (registration evidence), T7 (document content) and T13 (route) are documented; until then HOLD.
decisions.T4_nonEuBusiness: PROPOSED: B2B software licence service supplied where the business customer is established (§ 9(1) ZDPH); outside the scope of Czech VAT with the note 'Outside the scope of Czech VAT (§ 9(1) ZDPH)'. Foreign tax or nexus questions and the customer's business documentation are checked case by case. FIRST SALE: HOLD.
decisions.T5_businessStatusAndNoVatId: PROPOSED: The absence of a VAT ID does not settle whether an EU buyer is a taxable person; request documentary evidence (registration extract, business website, order on company letterhead) and review manually. FIRST SALE: HOLD. Consumers (B2C) are not sold to at all, and the code does NOT detect consumers automatically: there is no consumer category in lib/taxPolicy.js and classifyBuyer() never returns one. What the code does is refuse any order that is not placed as a business: the order form (lib/acceptance.js) requires the buyer company's legal name, its registration number, its country, a named individual with a role, and a separately ticked declaration that the individual is authorised to bind the company and that the purchase is made in the course of its business; without that declaration the order is not created (api/checkout.js), and the declaration is recorded on the order and printed in the agreement confirmation PDF. A consumer can therefore not knowingly proceed as an ordinary B2B order: to proceed at all, the buyer has to make a false business declaration. PRACTICAL IDENTITY CHECKS before fulfilment of the first sale: the registration number against the public register (justice.cz / ARES), the VAT ID where given (VIES / ARES), the billing country Stripe records against the declared country (onCountryMismatch: hold), the purchasing e-mail domain against the company. A purchase that nevertheless turns out to be by a consumer is cancelled and refunded under Refund Policy §4; no treatment category is needed for that because no consumer treatment is ever sold.
decisions.T6_licenceClassification: PROPOSED: Standard downloadable software is an electronically supplied service (Art. 7 Implementing Regulation (EU) 282/2011); the B2B general place-of-supply rule applies. Bespoke development, live consulting or mixed services are NOT covered by this policy and must not be sold under SKU CAI-L4-CI-001. The accountant confirms against the actual SKU and licence text.
decisions.T7_taxDocumentRequirements: PROPOSED: Every invoice identifies supplier (name, address, IČO, DIČ), customer (name, address, registration number, VAT ID if any), the supply (SKU, release, 'perpetual licence for one Microsoft tenant'), consideration (USD, and the CZK base in the records per T8), date of issue, a unique number, the payment reference and the tax note of the buyer category. TAX POINT (datum uskutečnění zdanitelného plnění): the licence is a service (provision of a right, § 14(1)(b) ZDPH) supplied when it is delivered, i.e. when the download becomes available (order.facts.fulfilledAt) - § 21(3) ZDPH. Payment is a separate fact (order.facts.paidAt). In the standard card flow the payment is confirmed seconds BEFORE delivery, so the consideration is received before the supply and § 20a(2) ZDPH fixes the tax point at the day the payment was received; both dates normally fall on the same day and then the two rules agree. The document (lib/invoicePdf.js, taxPointOf) prints the tax point with its basis AND the two dates separately ('Payment received', 'Licence delivered'); it never derives one from the other or from the issue date. Where delivery is NOT immediate (withheld or refused sale, bank transfer pending fulfilment) the document is for an advance payment, says 'licence not yet delivered', and the accountant decides whether a further document is issued on delivery. Historical orders keep the timestamps they recorded; nothing is rewritten. ACCOUNTANT TO CONFIRM: that for an identified person's domestic invoice without VAT the same date is used as the date of supply for accounting, and the advance-payment handling. EVIDENCE NEEDED: one real Stripe-generated invoice PDF from the test purchase, checked line by line against this list before T13 is approved.
decisions.T8_currencyConversion: PROPOSED: The contract price is in USD. For VAT records and the EC Sales List, USD is converted to CZK at the ČNB rate valid on the date of supply (§ 4(8) ZDPH); for accounting, at the rate the accounting policy fixes (daily ČNB rate, or the fixed rate for the period). The Stripe settlement/payout rate is NEVER the statutory conversion; it is recorded separately for bank reconciliation (scripts/commerce/reconcile-payout.mjs). The order record stores gross payment, the applicable rate, its source and date, the CZK value, and Stripe's payout amount and fees (invoice.conversion {rate, source, date, amountCzk}; printed on our own documents only when present). EVIDENCE NEEDED: the accountant's written choice of accounting rate method; then the rate source is wired into the invoicing route.
decisions.T9_revenueRecognition: PROPOSED: The one-off licence is recognised when delivered (download available = fulfilledAt). Corrective releases within the support window and e-mail support are a separately identified promise; the accountant decides whether a portion is deferred. Continuous Certification (not open) would be recognised over its period. EVIDENCE NEEDED: written accounting policy.
decisions.T10_partnerCommissions: PROPOSED: No partner commission on the first sale (CAI_PARTNER_PROGRAM off for the launch order). When commissions start, each partner's entity, residence, VAT status and contract decide the treatment (an EU-established partner's service is normally reverse-charged by the identified person; a Czech partner invoices under its own status). Not one rule for all.
decisions.T11_servicesFromAbroad: PROPOSED: A service received from a foreign business with place of supply in the Czech Republic (§ 9(1) ZDPH) is self-assessed by the identified person (§ 108(3) ZDPH) in the return for the month in which the obligation arose, due by the 25th of the following month, without input deduction. NOT every supplier fee is the same and NO invoice is reverse-charged automatically. URGENT - Microsoft invoice G195024562 (reported 30 Oct 2026, EUR 218.52 net + EUR 45.89 VAT): the following ORIGINAL fields determine the treatment and must be read from the document itself, not from the reported figures: (1) the supplier legal entity and its VAT number (e.g. Microsoft Ireland Operations Ltd, IE…; or a Czech VAT number CZ…) - this decides whether the supplier is foreign; (2) the customer block: which Colleague AI identifier is printed, and whether DIČ CZ29540852 appears - Microsoft invoices a customer with a validated VAT ID as a B2B reverse-charge supply and one without as a consumer supply with local VAT; (3) the VAT line: rate, amount and the country whose VAT it is (EUR 45.89 on EUR 218.52 is exactly 21 %, the Czech standard rate, which suggests Czech VAT was charged under the OSS/consumer treatment because no VAT ID was on the account) and any reverse-charge or 'VAT to be accounted for by the recipient' legend; (4) the date of issue and the service period or tax point stated (which month the obligation falls in); (5) the description of the service (cloud subscription, licence, marketplace fee); (6) the net amount and currency, and the CZK conversion rule for the return (T8); (7) the payment date. DECISION TREE for the accountant: if the supplier is foreign AND the invoice carries no VAT and the reverse-charge legend -> self-assess 21 % Czech VAT in the October 2026 return (due 25 Nov 2026), book no deduction. If the supplier is foreign AND charged Czech (or another EU) VAT because no VAT ID was registered on the account -> the supplier treated us as a non-taxable person; the VAT charged is not recoverable, the self-assessment obligation under § 108(3) still has to be assessed (the accountant decides whether it arises in addition), and the Microsoft account must be updated with DIČ CZ29540852 so that future invoices are reverse-charged. If the supplier is a Czech entity with a CZ VAT number -> a domestic supply with Czech VAT; no self-assessment, no deduction (not a VAT payer). Whether a return for October 2026 is due on 25 Nov 2026 follows from (1), (3) and (4) only; it is the accountant's call from the original. No amount is booked from this note.
decisions.T12_bankTransferProforma: PROPOSED: Bank transfer stays OFF for the first live sale (CAI_PAYMENT_METHODS=card). If enabled later: proforma (not a tax document) at order, invoice on receipt of payment, advance-payment and tax-point rules designed and approved separately.
decisions.T13_invoiceRoute: PROPOSED: The Stripe post-payment invoice is reused ONLY if a real Stripe-generated PDF from the Preview test purchase shows every T7 item (seller and buyer details, issue date, date of supply, unique number, the T3 note, no reverse-charge wording on a CZ document, archived copy on the order). Otherwise the Czech route (our own numbering, lib/invoicePdf.js, CZK per T8) is used. Stripe is not labelled compliant until that check is written up (docs/commerce/invoicing-route-assessment.md Q1-Q4).
decisions.T14_microsoftConsumption: PROPOSED: Microsoft bills Copilot Studio / Power Platform consumption to the customer directly under the customer's own Microsoft agreement; nothing is invoiced or re-charged by Colleague AI. The product facts, pricing page and licence say so consistently (verified 21 Nov 2026).

treatments._consumers: No consumer treatment exists in the code (lib/taxPolicy.js CATEGORIES) and none is added here: consumers are not sold to. Enforcement is the mandatory business declaration and identification on the order form (T5), not automatic detection. A consumer purchase discovered later is cancelled and refunded under Refund Policy §4.

checkout._note: stripeTax stays false unless a separate analysis establishes that Stripe Tax should calculate a tax; invoiceRoute 'stripe' is conditional on T13 and switches to the Czech route if the sample fails the T7 check.

turnoverMonitoring.rule: Czech VAT-payer thresholds for a calendar year: CZK 2,000,000 (payer from 1 January of the next year) and CZK 2,536,500 (payer from the day after the threshold is crossed), counting supplies with place of supply in the Czech Republic under § 4a ZDPH at the CZK value for the date of supply - not worldwide receipts, not Stripe payouts.
turnoverMonitoring.implementation: config/vat-thresholds.json (effectiveFrom, thresholds) + lib/vatTurnover.js + scripts/commerce/vat-turnover.mjs (read-only). Counts only supplies whose place of supply is the Czech Republic, read from the tax treatment recorded on the order at checkout (applied treatment, category cz_business); supplies to VAT-verified EU businesses and non-EU businesses are outside Czech turnover (§ 9(1) ZDPH) and are reported as excluded; everything else (pending or unverified VAT ID, no VAT ID, no applied treatment, no CZK conversion and no rate) is listed as UNRESOLVED for the accountant and the report never concludes 'ok' while an unresolved order exists. The year is the caller's or the current calendar year, never a constant. A threshold crossing is detected on the running gross total at the date of supply; a refund granted later does not undo it, and the net figure after refunds is reported beside the gross one. Warns at 80 % of the lower threshold.
turnoverMonitoring.cadence: run monthly with the VAT-return check and after every sale; the accountant confirms which supplies count.

expansion.note: All non-CZ categories remain in the matrix with their wording so that opening EU B2B (T2) or non-EU B2B (T4) later is a treatment change from hold to sell with the accountant's written confirmation, plus EC Sales List filing for T2. Nothing in the code assumes CZ-only.
